why_amended: Owner states the longer aug14 sets are deliberate: the objective is to EXTEND the field of view and FILL IN sky that currently has fewer layers stacked. That is a COVERAGE objective, and the original design measured SNR only — which can select the wrong arm for this goal.
the_tension_this_exposes: --weight=noise down-weights july31's members by up to 2.56x. Where many nights overlap deeply that maximises SNR and costs nothing. But in THIN-coverage edge sky — precisely the zones the owner wants filled — a down-weighted contributor reduces EFFECTIVE DEPTH. So the arm that wins on SNR could lose on the stated objective, and the original decision rule would not have detected it.

instrument_refinement.why: weighting changes NOISE and cannot change SIGNAL: both arms are linear combinations of the SAME members under the same -norm=addscale, so the signal term is identical and the SNR ratio between arms IS the inverse noise ratio. A (signal-sky)/noise ratio built on 6% contrast is dominated by box choice — my first pair returned NEGATIVE SNR because the nominal 'sky' box was brighter than the nominal 'signal' box. The bgnoise field carries the hypothesis's actual quantity and is not sensitive to box placement.
instrument_refinement.not_a_goalpost_move: recorded BEFORE the corpus arms ran, and it does not change the hypothesis, the arms, the prediction (+5.43%) or the decision thresholds — only which field of the same instrument's output estimates the predicted quantity.

the_prediction_was_WRONG_and_here_is_why.broken_assumption: the pre-registration modelled member variance as proportional to SKY LEVEL (background-limited, sigma ~ sqrt(sky)). It named this as the assumption most likely to fail, but blamed READ NOISE. Read noise is not the reason.
the_prediction_was_WRONG_and_here_is_why.MEASURED_mechanism: members are ALREADY STACKED under -norm=addscale, so normalisation absorbs most of the sky difference BEFORE the compose sees it. Siril bgnoise on real members: july31 2.902-2.938 (green) against aug06 2.406-2.663 — a 1.22x noise spread from a 2.56x SKY spread, where sqrt(sky) predicts 1.60x.
the_prediction_was_WRONG_and_here_is_why.corrected_model: re-running the same variance arithmetic with MEASURED member noise instead of the sky proxy predicts +0.673% — same order as the +0.188% measured, and firmly inside NULL. The residual 0.67 vs 0.19 is within the crudeness of using one member's noise per night as that night's representative.

durable_finding: SKY LEVEL IS NOT A PROXY FOR MEMBER NOISE ON THIS ROUTE. A 2.56x sky spread arrives at the compose as a 1.22x noise spread because every member is a normalised stack. So nbstack and noise are near-equivalent for ANY corpus built this way, and run_undistort_compose.sh's own guidance ('prefer noise for a MULTI-NIGHT compose, where sky brightness differs between members') is TRUE IN PRINCIPLE and IMMATERIAL IN PRACTICE here — the premise it rests on (per-frame noise differing between members) is largely cancelled upstream. That is why run_corpus_combine.sh's nbstack default, which looked like an unreviewed oversight from the commit dates, costs nothing measurable.
what_this_does_NOT_say: it does not show nbstack is CORRECT in general — only that the two are indistinguishable at this corpus's 1.22x member-noise spread. A corpus with genuinely unequal member noise would separate them, and the corrected model is the way to predict whether it is worth testing.
it does not test the OWNER'S coverage objective — depth in thin-edge sky was measured separately and is not a function of this knob at NULL.

A_METHOD_ERROR_CAUGHT_BEFORE_IT_BECAME_A.why_it_matters_beyond_this_run: any comparison of two products whose members differ in geometry has this bias, and it points in the direction of whichever product was cropped.

THE_CROP_DAMAGES_NO_MEMBER: the decisive control. The SAME member measured at the SAME sky, uncropped vs cropped: aug14/set-04 sub_04 FWHM 3.435 -> 3.430 and roundness 0.658 -> 0.654; sub_05 3.405 -> 3.405, 0.659 -> 0.658; sub_06 3.335 -> 3.333, 0.688 -> 0.694. THE_MECHANISM.1: at the union's rim, a member covers that sky only via a band near its OWN frame edge — the band the 5%/side crop deletes.
THE_MECHANISM.2: MEASURED at the defect sky (RA 326.68, Dec 39.45), distance from the member's nearest x edge, control -> cropped: aug06/set-02 sub_04 370 px -> 73 px (reduced to a sliver); aug14/set-01 sub_05 400 px -> 97 px (sliver); aug14/set-03 sub_05 286 px -> OUTSIDE ENTIRELY; aug14/set-04 sub_04 600 px -> 302 px (survives comfortably).
THE_MECHANISM.3: so the contributors do not thin evenly — the ones whose reach came from their frame edge are dropped, and the ones that had that sky further inside survive.
THE_MECHANISM.4: AT THIS SKY THE SURVIVORS ARE THE POOR ONES. Per-member PSF there: aug06/set-02 sub_04 FWHM 2.735 roundness 0.814; aug14/set-01 sub_05 2.958 / 0.743; aug14/set-04 sub_04/05/06 3.34-3.44 / 0.654-0.694. The control blends 7 members from 4 sets including the good ones; the arm keeps 2-3 members from ONE set, the poor ones. The composite tracks its contributors: 3.257 -> 3.487.
THE_MECHANISM.5: NOT A BAD SET. At centre sky every set measures FWHM 2.25-2.68 and roundness 0.943-0.971, with aug14/set-04 the ROUNDEST (2.547 / 0.971). The degradation is sky-position-specific, not set quality — so it cannot be fixed by culling a set.

THE_RULE_THIS_ESTABLISHES.statement: at a max-framed union's rim, the frame EDGES are what supply contributor DIVERSITY. Cropping every frame removes the overlap that let good members reach the rim, and whichever set still reaches there dominates it alone.
THE_RULE_THIS_ESTABLISHES.quantified: median dFWHM +0.133 px at the 7 sweep positions that lose >=2 contributing SETS, against +0.012 px at the 23 that lose fewer — an 11x difference. Member COUNT alone does not predict it; SET diversity does.
THE_RULE_THIS_ESTABLISHES.why_it_is_the_opposite_of_the_hypothesis: the crop was expected to stop the union amplifying each frame's worst part. At the rim it does the reverse: it removes the diverse good contributors and concentrates the region onto whatever single set survives.

MY_MEASUREMENT_WAS_BLIND_TO_IT_AND_THAT_: the shared-sky grid admitted a position only where an 800 px box fits WHOLLY INSIDE BOTH canvases. That rule structurally excludes the arm's rim — the earlier record even states 'rim n=0' — which is precisely the zone a frame crop damages. The comparison was therefore sound about what it measured and silent about where the defect lives. ANY comparison of a cropped product against its uncropped parent must sample the cropped product's OWN rim, not only the shared interior. The owner found by eye what the grid could not.

status: TESTED AND REFUTED at the member level; successor hypothesis formed from the same measurement
question: the crop5lr stacks read a +8.3% additive background pedestal vs their controls (constant at every sky position, bgnoise unchanged, output-norm excluded via 0.08% maxima agreement). Where does it enter?
hypothesis_A_refuted: group-stack `-norm=addscale` anchors on frame statistics; cropping removes the vignetting-darkened edge columns from those statistics, shifting every cropped frame's median up. PREDICTION: every crop member reads ~+8% background vs its full-chain twin at the same stars. MEASURED: Siril findstar per-star local background B at ~1800 pattern-matched star pairs per member, 35 member twins (the committed msep lists, no new tool runs): median B_arm/B_ctrl = 0.9976 — NO member-level pedestal. Refuted.
what_the_same_measurement_showed: per-member anchor SCATTER is huge: B_arm/B_ctrl ranges 0.75-1.15 across members (IQR 0.90-1.01). Each group-stack's additive normalization anchors on the group's own internal reference frame, and the two chains' group registrations chose their references independently — so member background levels are chain-lottery, roughly +-15%.
hypothesis_B_open: the COMPOSE also normalizes additively against its pinned reference member (run_undistort_compose docstring: -norm=addscale drives the composite's balance). An additive norm maps every member to the reference's level, so the composed stack's background = the reference member's anchor - and the +8.3% pedestal is the difference between the two arms' reference members' anchor levels, a per-build lottery draw, not a systematic of the crop. Consistent with the measured scatter; explains why the pedestal is constant across sky.
test_for_B: Siril stat backgrounds: each composed stack vs its own reference member at matched sky (4-6 stat calls) - queued behind the running corpus build (siril lock). Also predicts the aug14 cross-night pair's pedestal equals its ref-pair anchor difference (ref s_00016 measured ~1.00 twin ratio, so that pair's pedestal should be small - checkable the same way).
consequence_bound: an additive constant cancels in SPCC's local-annulus photometry and under the sky-anchored per-product stretch; with crop5lr retired no shipping route carries the crop side. The open question is now about COMPOSE REFERENCE ANCHORING generally - if hypothesis B holds, every combine's absolute background level is a function of reference choice, which the sky-anchored render doctrine already absorbs.

the two chains' reference members differ by MORE than the composites do (R 1.38 vs 1.24, G 1.22 vs 1.09, B 1.27 vs 1.13) - so the composite does NOT simply inherit the reference's anchor: hypothesis B as stated is refuted
member anchors differing 22-38% between chains at the reference pair confirms the anchor-lottery finding at its extreme (the matched-star scan showed +-15% IQR-ish scatter)
surviving_mechanism_space: normalization-family: the compose's -norm=addscale maps members toward the reference but the composite lands PART WAY between unity and the reference ratio, so either the additive coefficients are computed over overlap statistics the crop changed, or -output_norm rescales after, or the plain mean of imperfectly-equalized members averages the anchors. The arithmetic of addscale + output_norm + mean over 13 members is the open question; the consequence bound stands (SPCC local-annulus photometry and the per-product sky-anchored stretch absorb constant per-channel offsets).
